passage:
A restaurant used digital menus that changed based on ingredient availability. If fish sold out, the dish disappeared from the menu automatically.
Customers liked accurate information. But some older customers preferred paper menus and found screens tiring.
The restaurant offered both. It also used the digital system to reduce food waste by promoting dishes with ingredients that needed to be used soon.
The manager said technology should serve the meal, not become the meal.
The menu taught a simple business lesson. Innovation is useful when it solves real problems without forgetting different customers. A restaurant still begins with hospitality.
